canonical.title: Audit the research plan before the first session

required_sources.note: the study overview; nothing else is needed for this prompt

steps.text: Read the research plan. Restate the key decision this study informs in one sentence, and list every hypothesis and research question it names. If the decision, the hypotheses, and the research questions do not connect to each other, say exactly where the chain breaks.

For each hypothesis, state what observation in a session would count as evidence against it. If no session observation could disprove a hypothesis, rewrite it as a falsifiable statement and flag the rewrite as your own.
List any research question that the planned sessions and sample cannot answer, and suggest the smallest change (sample, segment, or question) that would close the gap.

canonical.title: Scan the plan for leading questions

required_sources.note: the study overview holds the hypotheses the questions must stay neutral against

steps.text: Read the research plan and list every place where the wording assumes the hypothesis is true, invites a polite answer, or names the team's preferred solution. Quote each spot.
Rewrite each quoted spot as a neutral, open question a participant cannot answer by agreeing. Mark the rewrites as suggestions; the plan is not edited by this prompt.

canonical.title: Find what the latest sessions did not cover

required_sources.note: the session summaries already uploaded for this study; run after each debrief
needed to name the research questions; warn and ask before continuing without it

steps.text: For each research question in the plan, name the sessions that touched it and one sentence on what they showed. Answer only from the session summaries, never from memory of the topic.
List the research questions no session has touched yet, and the questions only one session has touched. For each, suggest the probe to raise in the next session.

canonical.title: Contrast the two most recent sessions

required_sources.note: at least two session summaries must be uploaded

steps.text: Take the two most recently uploaded session summaries. List what both participants said that points the same way, with one short quote from each.
List what they said that points in opposite directions. For each split, state what difference in role, workflow, or setup best explains it, and mark the explanation as a guess.

canonical.title: Weigh the evidence behind each claim

required_sources.note: all session summaries for the study

steps.text: List every distinct claim the session summaries support. For each claim, name every session that supports it and count the sources.
Mark each claim backed by a single session as single-source. For each single-source claim, state exactly what the next session should check to confirm or drop it.

canonical.title: Read the outliers before they harden into themes

required_sources.note: all session summaries; useful from three sessions onward

steps.text: State the view that most sessions share on each research question.

List every statement that contradicts that majority view, with its session and a quote. For each, say whether it reads as a different context, a different role, or a one-off, and what evidence would settle which.

canonical.title: Check the summaries carry no direct identifiers

required_sources.note: the session summaries are the only uploads that could hold participant detail

steps.text: Scan every session summary for email addresses, phone numbers, exact account names, or other direct identifiers of the participant. List each finding with its session.
For each finding, state whether the session summary can keep it (public role title, generic account description) or should replace it (contact detail, exact account name), and with what wording.

required_sources.note: all session summaries; the more sessions, the stronger the themes
needed to tie themes back to the research questions; warn and ask before continuing without it

steps.text: Propose themes that answer the research questions. Each theme needs a one-sentence statement, the sessions that evidence it, and one quote per session. No theme may rest on a paraphrase alone.
Label each theme emerging (one or two sessions), developing (three or four), or saturated (five or more), and list the codes inside each theme.
List evidence that fits no theme. Say whether it is noise or a theme the study did not plan for, and what a follow-up study would need to test it.

required_sources.note: the hypotheses and assumptions live in the plan

steps.text: For each hypothesis in the plan, answer Supports, Challenges, or Mixed, then give the strongest single quote for that verdict and name its session. Where evidence is absent, say Insufficient evidence; do not stretch a quote to reach a verdict.
For each assumption in the plan, answer Holds, Breaks, or Untested this session, with the session that settles it. An assumption no session touched stays Untested.

canonical.title: Frame the findings against the key decision

required_sources.note: the key decision the study serves

steps.text: Restate the key decision. For each finding, state what it changes about that decision: proceed, change the approach, or needs more evidence. Keep each to two sentences and cite the sessions behind it.
List the smallest set of next actions the findings support, each tied to a finding. Mark any action that rests on single-source evidence as preliminary.

required_sources.note: all session summaries; run after the theme draft

steps.text: Take the strongest finding from the themes. Write the best case that it is wrong: what would the sessions have to show, and is any of that already present in them? Quote anything that supports the opposite case.
State the single observation in a future session that would most weaken the finding. If no observation could weaken it, say the finding is unfalsifiable as worded and rewrite it.

For each finding, rate confidence high (three or more sessions agree), medium (two sessions), or low (one session), and name the strongest quote and its session. Table: finding, confidence, sessions, quote.
List which findings are ready for the report and which need another session first. A low-confidence finding is report-ready only when labeled single-source and preliminary.

personal_extras.title: Audio overview of the study so far
personal_extras.text: Create an audio overview of this notebook that walks through the research plan and every session summary so far, in order, ending with the open questions.

personal_extras.title: Stakeholder recap paragraph
personal_extras.text: Write one paragraph for a busy stakeholder: what we asked, what participants did, and the one thing that should change. No research vocabulary, no session labels, no participant names.

personal_extras.title: Quote bank for the report
personal_extras.text: List the ten clearest participant quotes across all session summaries, each with its session and what finding it supports. Keep participant wording exactly as written in the summaries.
